Cost: 2 Investiture

Choice is a privilege. He withdraws it.

Spend 2 Investiture and choose a Compelled, Frightened, or Weakened character in Attunement Range. Test Black vs. Cognitive. On a success, you choose the target's action on its next turn (the target cannot be forced to directly harm itself). On a failure, the target is Weakened until the end of its next turn.

AbsAuthTest00000.description: Power. 07-24q: replaced a preUseItem TAKEOVER (iron rule 2b). Black vs the target's Cognitive, player-rolled per Ben's ruling. `requireTargetStatus` is H1's new field and it is what made this talent convertible — the compelled/frightened/weakened gate is enforced BEFORE cost, so the hand-rolled "nothing spent" guarantee survives.

AbsAuthWin000000.description: Power. Forced volition has no Foundry hook (audit §9k, the D10 class), so the success stays table-run — but as an editable rule, not a name-keyed ChatMessage.create.

handler.text: you choose the target's action on its next turn — it cannot be forced to directly harm itself. Forced volition, GM-run.

AbsAuthFail00000.description: Power. THE FIRST CONSUMER OF `edha-test-fail` IN THE PROJECT. The event was built in pass D and dispatched to nothing for four passes; the consolation Weakened is what it was built for. Expiry is TARGET-relative (end of ITS next turn), not owner.

Defy and bleed. He has worn the crown a long time.

Spend 2 Investiture. For the scene, when one of your Black or Red talents tests against a character's Cognitive, that character takes spirit damage equal to your Presence. This damage cannot be reduced.

CrownArm00000000.description: Power. 07-24q (H8): arms the crown for the scene. A STATUS, not the old bespoke `crownActive` flag — a status is the one arming marker a document-driven rule can both write (this rule) and read (the watch rule below), and it shows on the token so "am I armed?" stops being a memory test. The generic already-armed veto refuses a second use before cost.

CrownNote0000000.description: Power. The card, including the MANUAL surface. The engine hears every test H1 resolves; a Black/Red vs-Cognitive test the engine did NOT resolve (GM-adjudicated, or a talent not yet on H1) still has to reach the crown, so the button re-announces it by hand. The button is generic — it carries the observation as data attributes and names no talent.

handler.text: armed for the scene: whenever one of your Black or Red talents tests against a character's Cognitive, that character takes spirit = Presence — automatically on any engine-resolved test. For a Black/Red vs-Cognitive test the engine did not resolve: target the character, then click.

CrownWatch000000.description: Power. THE CONVERSION. Crown of Thorns is a rider on a test resolved by a DIFFERENT talent on the same actor — the shape neither event system could express, because a rule only ever sees its own item's events (audit §9o). `whenOutcome: any` is deliberate: the crown bites whether the test landed or not.

CrownPing0000000.description: Power. The payload: spirit = Presence. Spirit bypasses deflect, which is what the card's "cannot be reduced" means — no special handling needed.

He does not raise his voice. The voice is enough.

Spend 1 Investiture and choose a character in Attunement Range. Test Black vs. Cognitive. On a success, the target is Compelled until the start of your next turn; while Compelled, the target must spend its next action either moving toward you or doing nothing. You have an advantage on attack tests against any Compelled, Frightened, or Weakened character in Attunement Range.

Cost: 3 Investiture

He wears the crown not yet given. The world fits anyway.

Spend 3 Investiture. For the scene, you gain +2 to all defenses and your melee attacks deal additional spirit damage equal to your tier. Allies in Attunement Range gain +1 to all tests. When you take damage, you may redirect up to your tier of that damage to one or more willing allies in Attunement Range. Once per scene.

Cost: 2 Investiture

The hand grows certain. The blade grows hungry.

Spend 2 Investiture. For the scene, your melee attacks deal additional damage equal to the number of characters you have reduced below half their maximum HP during this scene, to a maximum bonus equal to your tier x 2. When you reduce a character to 0 HP, this bonus immediately increases by 1 (still capped at tier x 2).
